title: Space Reservations
subtitle: How to book the Cafegym, the ES Turf and the Kinder Playground — and how requests get approved.

slides.title: Scan to open this deck

steps.h: Point your camera at the code
steps.b: Or open coachkenny.org/decks and tap this deck.
Same slides as the projector — swipe at your own pace.
The link opens slide 1 of this Space Reservations walkthrough.

slides.note: Hold here until every phone shows the deck.

slides.title: Reserving a space
slides.lede: What every teacher and staff member does. Five steps, about a minute.

slides.title: Sign in
slides.lede: Go to slamnvreserve.org. Leave "Sign in as" on Staff Teacher, type your school email, and press Confirm Email.

steps.b: It confirms your @slamnv.org Google account. A personal Gmail will be turned away.

slides.title: Check what is already booked
slides.lede: The calendar opens first on purpose — look before you request, and you will avoid most conflicts.

steps.h: The dot tells you the space
steps.b: Red is the Cafegym, green is the ES Turf, grey is the Kinder Playground. Same colors in the sidebar.
Click an empty day and it jumps straight into the request form with that date already filled in.

slides.title: Tell it who you are
slides.lede: Your name, then your building — and the building opens up to show every role in it.

steps.h: Pick your building, then your exact role
steps.b: Elementary, Middle School, High School, or Coach — then the specific role in it.
Choosing Coach unlocks the repeating practice schedule builder — that is Part 2.

slides.title: Say what it is for
slides.lede: Keep it short — this text becomes the calendar event title everyone else sees.

steps.b: “Popsicle Party” reads better on a shared calendar than a paragraph.
Tap a common one — Popsicle Party, Water Day, Fingerpainting, Tie Dye Party — instead of typing.

slides.title: Choose the space
slides.lede: One space per request. Need the Cafegym and the Turf on the same day? Submit two requests.

steps.b: Indoor. The busiest space by far, and the one with the most approvers watching it.
Outdoor. Usually much more open.

slides.title: Add your dates and times
slides.lede: One request can carry as many dates as you need — add them one at a time and they stack up in a list.

steps.h: Set the date, start and end
steps.b: Then press Add Date. Repeat for each one you want.
If three of your four dates are clear, those three get approved and only the fourth gets flagged.

slides.title: Review, then submit
slides.lede: Last look before it goes to the approver. The preview card on the right has been tracking along the whole time.

steps.b: Name, space, and every date and time you added.

steps.h: Go back if you need to
steps.b: Nothing is submitted until you press Submit Request.

slides.title: Submitted — now it is pending
slides.lede: You are finished. Two emails go out immediately: a confirmation to you, and a notification to the approver.

steps.b: It does not appear on the shared calendar until it is approved.

steps.h: You will hear back by email
steps.b: Approved, denied with a reason, or flagged as a conflict — then a calendar invite lands automatically.

slides.title: Coaches: a whole season at once
slides.lede: Instead of adding thirty practice dates by hand, describe the pattern and let it build the schedule.

slides.title: Choose Coach
slides.lede: Coach sits alongside the three buildings. Pick it and the rest of the form switches into season mode.

slides.title: Practice or Banquet
slides.lede: Coaches get two booking types instead of a free-text purpose box.

steps.b: Opens the repeating schedule builder — pick days of the week and a season range.
A one-off event. It behaves like a normal teacher request from here.

slides.title: Describe the pattern once
slides.lede: This is the part that saves the most time. Pick your days, set the times, give it a season, and press Generate.

steps.h: Tap your days, set your times
steps.b: Up to five a week — Monday can run 3:30–5:00 and Wednesday 4:00–5:30, each day keeps its own start and end.
Set the season range and press Generate Schedule.
Any date on the Holidays list is skipped automatically and it tells you how many it removed.

slides.note: Six dates from four taps — and you can still delete any single one

slides.title: One request, every date
slides.lede: The whole season submits together and stays grouped for the approver, who can clear it in one action.

steps.b: The approver gets a single notification listing the full schedule — clear dates get approved, only collisions get flagged.

slides.title: The approver side
slides.lede: Where requests get approved, denied, or flagged — and where the calendar events actually get created.

slides.title: Sign in as Staff Admin
slides.lede: Same login screen as everyone else — switch "Sign in as" to Staff Admin and a password field appears.

steps.b: Staff Admin adds a password field under the email box.
Your address has to be on the approver list — a correct password alone will not get you in.

slides.title: See everything at a glance
slides.lede: Four counts across the top, then the queue. Conflicts are sorted to the front because they need a decision.

steps.b: Click Conflicts to see only conflicts. Click it again to clear.
Needs Review is your working queue. All Requests is the full history.

slides.title: Clear a whole season at once
slides.lede: Expand a coach season and you can approve every clear date in one press, or cherry-pick with checkboxes.

steps.b: Press ✓ All on the header row to approve every pending date without even expanding it.
Expand, tick the dates you want, then Approve Selected or Deny Selected.

slides.note: Denying in bulk asks once for a reason and sends it on every date

slides.title: Look at a conflict properly
slides.lede: Press Review on any request and you get the details next to a live calendar for that space.

steps.b: The purple pin is what is being asked for; the colored bars are what is already booked.
Approve anyway, deny it, or send a conflict email asking the teacher to pick another slot.

slides.title: Deny with a reason
slides.lede: A reason is required, and it goes to the teacher word for word — so write something they can act on.

steps.b: “Turf is booked for the track meet that morning, try another day or the Cafegym” beats “denied”.

steps.h: They can retry in one click
steps.b: The denial email includes a Submit New Request link straight back to the form.

slides.title: Approved — and it is on the calendar
slides.lede: Approving is the moment the booking becomes real. Everything after this is automatic.

steps.h: The event gets created and everyone is invited
steps.b: It lands on that space’s own Google Calendar. The teacher is added as a guest — Cafegym bookings also invite the three Cafegym approvers.

slides.title: What happens without anyone doing it
slides.lede: The parts of this that used to be somebody’s job.

cards.b: Every date is checked against that space’s calendar when it is submitted — and checked again when it is approved.
Approving creates the Google Calendar event on the right space calendar. Nobody types it in twice.
The requester is invited automatically, so it lands on their own calendar. Cafegym also invites its three approvers.
Dates on the Holidays sheet are dropped out of generated coach schedules before they are ever submitted.
Submitted, approved, denied with a reason, and conflict notices — all sent automatically with a link back.
Requests whose date has already passed are removed from the sheet on their own.

columns.k: If you are booking a space
items: Look at the calendar first — most conflicts die right here.
Sign in with your @slamnv.org email as Staff Teacher.
Name, building, role. Keep the purpose to a few words.
Add every date you need in one request.
Watch your email — it is not booked until it is approved.
Tap your practice days — up to five a week.
Give each day its own start and end time.
Set the season range and press Generate Schedule.
Holidays are already removed. Submit once.
Sign in as Staff Admin with your password.
Work the Needs Review tab; conflicts float to the top.
Coach seasons: ✓ All clears every pending date.
Press Review to see a conflict against the space calendar.
Denying needs a reason — the teacher reads it verbatim.
